comment: OrangeHRM demo, the Leave module end to end: setup logs in and seeds an employee 'Jevtest Leave${RUN_STAMP}' with plain Playwright (PIM > Add Employee), then Jev opens Leave, Assign Leave, picks the employee through the autocomplete (whose list first shows a 'Searching....' placeholder row for about a second), a leave type from a custom dropdown, types the date into From Date in the demo's yyyy-dd-mm format (2026-14-10 is Wednesday 14 October 2026; the demo's work week is Monday to Friday and its holiday list is Canada's, so 2026-10-10, a Saturday, and 2026-11-11, Remembrance Day, were both answered with the toast 'Failed to Submit: No Working Days Selected', the app's correct refusal) before choosing the leave type, because typing a date opens a calendar popup and the next click only closes it (the second run clicked Assign into that popup, the form re-rendered with a Duration field and nothing was submitted), clicks Assign and confirms the 'Balance not sufficient' dialog a new employee always gets. The module lands on Leave List, and a saved assignment does not redirect there (the form is shown again, emptied; the first version of this spec said it redirected, and one run then hesitated between re-filling the form and the Leave List tab until low_confidence), so reaching that page proves nothing (the first version passed on the landing page alone): the pass is the assignment found in the Leave List table after filtering by the employee and the status Scheduled, and the no_records outcome requires those filters to be set (the unfiltered list says 'No Records Found' too). min_confidence 0.55 turns a marginal click on a transient row into a wait. ${RUN_STAMP} (a fresh value the runner makes up every run) keeps the employee unique. The no_records outcome fired once on the unfiltered list before Search was clicked although the filter checks read 0.82 / 0.88, so it now also has after: {click: Search}; the Assign form's toasts ('Successfully Saved', 'Failed to Submit: ...') faded before every observation and are now captured as announcements.
goal: Open Leave from the sidebar, then Assign Leave from the top row. Type the given employee name, wait for the suggestion with that name and choose it; type the given date into From Date and, if it is still empty, into To Date; open the Leave Type dropdown and choose the given leave type; click Assign, and if the form is still shown without any message, click Assign once more; click Ok in the 'Balance not sufficient' dialog. Then click Leave List in the top row (the Assign Leave form stays on screen, emptied, after Ok), and on the Leave List page open the 'Show Leave with Status' box and choose 'Scheduled', type the given employee name in the Employee Name filter and choose its suggestion, and click Search, so that the table shows exactly one leave record for 'Jevtest Leave${RUN_STAMP}' with the status Scheduled.
notes: The left sidebar lists the modules (Admin, PIM, Leave, Time, ...); its Search box only filters the menu entries: never type into it. Forms in this app load behind a spinner for a moment after a route change: type only once the fields are shown. Leave's top row has Apply, My Leave, Entitlements, Reports, Configure, Leave List and Assign Leave. Fields labelled 'Type for hints...' are autocompletes: type the given text, wait for the suggestion list, then click the suggestion that reads the full name before doing anything else; a value only typed and not chosen is rejected as 'Invalid'. While the suggestions load, the list shows a single row reading 'Searching....': that is a placeholder, never click it; wait until the row with the full name appears (about a second), then click that row. If the field shows a red 'Invalid', type the name again and wait for the suggestion. Dropdowns showing '-- Select --' open on click and list their options; click the option named in the data. Dates are typed as text in the form yyyy-dd-mm exactly as given in data (a working day: the given date is Wednesday 14 October 2026). Typing a date opens a calendar popup under the field; the next click anywhere only closes that popup, so choose the leave type after the dates, and if a click on Assign leaves the form unchanged (a Duration field showing 'Full Day' appears, no dialog, no message), click Assign again. To Date usually fills itself with the From Date. The employee has no leave balance, so after Assign a dialog titled 'Balance not sufficient' asks to confirm: click Ok. A green 'Successfully Saved' toast then shows briefly and the Assign Leave form is shown again, emptied (Leave Type back to '-- Select --'): the assignment is saved, do not fill the form again; click Leave List in the top row, the tab left of Assign Leave. Leave List opens with the status filter showing the chip 'Pending Approval' and 'No Records Found' below: that list is not the result. The 'Show Leave with Status' box is a multi-select: click its '-- Select --' area to open the options and click 'Scheduled'; 'Pending Approval' may stay selected. The table columns are Date, Employee Name, Leave Type, Leave Balance, Number of Days, Status.

checks.on_assign_form: The page heading says 'Assign Leave' and shows Employee Name, Leave Type, From Date and To Date
checks.balance_dialog: A popup dialog with the title 'Balance not sufficient' and the buttons Cancel and Ok is shown over the form
checks.on_leave_list: The page heading says 'Leave List' and shows the filters From Date, To Date, Show Leave with Status and Employee Name
checks.filter_scheduled: The 'Show Leave with Status' filter shows a chip reading 'Scheduled'
checks.filter_employee: The Employee Name filter on the Leave List contains 'Jevtest Leave${RUN_STAMP}'

leave_scheduled.when: The Leave List table shows a row with the employee name 'Jevtest Leave${RUN_STAMP}' and the status 'Scheduled'. A line says '(1) Record Found'

no_records.when: The Leave List says 'No Records Found' below the filters
no_records.note: the assignment was confirmed (Ok in the balance dialog) but the Scheduled leave is not listed for the employee

assign_error.when: A red 'Required', 'Invalid' or 'Should be' message is shown under a field of the Assign Leave form after Assign was clicked
assign_error.note: every field was given a valid value; check the trace for the field the app rejected

save_failed.when: A red toast says 'Failed to Submit' or 'Error'
save_failed.note: the app refused the assignment after Ok; 'No Working Days Selected' means the date in data is a weekend or holiday, which is a spec problem, any other reason is the app's

app_error.when: An error page, a stack trace or 'something went wrong' text is shown
